verses.text: "Have your brother Aaron and his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar brought to you from among the people of Israel, so that they can serve me as priests.
Make holy clothes for your brother Aaron, to give him honour and beauty.
Speak to all the skilled workers, whom I have filled with wisdom. Tell them to make clothes for Aaron, to set him apart as holy, so that he can serve me as priest.

These are the clothes they are to make: a chest piece, an ephod, a robe, a woven shirt, a turban, and a sash. They are to make these holy clothes for your brother Aaron and his sons, so that they can serve me as priests.
Have them use gold, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine linen.
Have them make the ephod of gold, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine twisted linen, the work of a skilled worker.
It is to have two shoulder pieces fastened to its two corners, so that it can be tied together.
Its skilfully woven belt must be made the same way and be one piece with it, of gold, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine twisted linen.
Take two onyx stones and carve on them the names of the sons of Israel.
Put six names on one stone and the other six on the other stone, in the order they were born.
Carve the names of the sons of Israel on the two stones the way a jeweller carves a seal. Then put the stones in gold settings.
Fasten the two stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, as stones to remind God of the sons of Israel. Aaron is to carry their names on his shoulders in front of the LORD, as a reminder.
Make gold settings,
and two chains of pure gold, twisted like a rope. Fasten the chains to the settings.
Make a chest piece for making decisions, the work of a skilled worker. Make it like the ephod, of gold, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine twisted linen.
It is to be square, folded double, about twenty-three centimetres long and twenty-three centimetres wide.
Put four rows of precious stones on it. In the first row put a ruby, a topaz, and a beryl.
In the second row put a turquoise, a sapphire, and an emerald.
In the third row put a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst.
In the fourth row put a chrysolite, an onyx, and a jasper. Set them in gold settings.
There are to be twelve stones, one for each of the names of the sons of Israel. Each stone is to be carved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
For the chest piece, make chains of pure gold, twisted like a rope.
Make two gold rings and fasten them to the two upper corners of the chest piece.
Fasten the two gold chains to the two rings at the corners of the chest piece.
Fasten the other ends of the chains to the two settings, and attach them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
Make two gold rings and fasten them to the other two corners of the chest piece, on the inside edge next to the ephod.
Make two more gold rings and fasten them to the bottom of the shoulder pieces on the front of the ephod, close to the seam just above its woven belt.
Tie the rings of the chest piece to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so that the chest piece sits above the woven belt and does not swing out from the ephod.
Whenever Aaron goes into the Holy Place, he will carry the names of the sons of Israel over his heart on the chest piece for making decisions. It will always remind the LORD of them.

Put the Urim and the Thummim in the chest piece, so that they will be over Aaron's heart whenever he goes in to the LORD. So Aaron will always carry over his heart the means of making decisions for the people of Israel in front of the LORD.
Make the robe of the ephod all of blue cloth.
It is to have an opening for the head in the middle, with a woven edge around the opening like a collar, so that it will not tear.
Around the bottom hem of the robe make pomegranates of blue, purple, and red yarn, with gold bells between them.
A gold bell and a pomegranate, a gold bell and a pomegranate, are to go all around the hem of the robe.
Aaron must wear it when he serves as priest. The sound of the bells will be heard when he goes into the Holy Place in front of the LORD and when he comes out, so that he will not die.
Make a plate of pure gold, and carve on it like a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD.
Fasten it with a blue cord to the front of the turban.

It will be on Aaron's forehead. Aaron will carry the guilt of any wrong in the holy gifts the people of Israel set apart. It will always be on his forehead, so that their gifts will be accepted by the LORD.
Weave the shirt of fine linen, and make the turban of fine linen. The sash is to be the work of someone who sews beautiful patterns.
Make shirts, sashes, and caps for Aaron's sons too, to give them honour and beauty.
Put these clothes on your brother Aaron and his sons. Then anoint them, ordain them, and set them apart as holy, so that they can serve me as priests.
Make linen underwear for them to cover their bodies, reaching from the waist to the thigh.

Aaron and his sons must wear them whenever they go into the Tent of Meeting, or come near the altar to serve in the Holy Place, so that they do not become guilty and die. This is a law that will last forever for Aaron and his descendants after him."
